title: Spatial Autocorrelation & Moran’s I
interviewAnswer: Spatial autocorrelation asks whether nearby observations are more similar than expected. Moran’s I is a common global measure; local indicators identify spatial clusters/outliers.
why: Geography often violates the independence assumption behind ordinary statistics.
intuition: Nearby house prices or disease rates often move together.
deepDive: A spatial weights matrix defines neighborhood structure; Moran’s I compares neighboring deviations with overall variance and commonly uses permutation inference.
commonMistakes: Choosing weights after seeing the desired result.
production: Define neighborhoods from domain logic and account for spatial dependence in inference/validation.
workedExample: A high-high cluster can identify adjacent regions with consistently elevated values.
